title: The State-Prediction Separation Hypothesis
abstract: arXiv:2607.01218v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Transformers use the same forward computation stream to both predict the next token and store useful state for future token predictions. We formulate the state-prediction separation hypothesis: disentangling the two roles yields better language modeling performance. We design a Transformer variant that uses separate computation streams to separate the two functions, and conduct pretraining experiments across various scales. Our experiments show that state-prediction separation consistently offers better data- and compute-efficiency, improving validation loss and outperforming standard Transformers by 2-3 percentage points on average on downstream tasks. We also conduct extensive empirical analysis that rules out potential confounders and demonstrates the fundamental difference in the gradients our design entails.

translated_abstract: Transformer 使用同一条前向计算流来同时完成两个任务：预测下一个 token，以及为未来的 token 预测存储有用的状态。我们提出了状态-预测分离假设：将这两种角色解耦能够带来更好的语言建模性能。我们设计了一种使用独立计算流来分离这两种功能的 Transformer 变体，并在多种规模上开展了预训练实验。实验表明，状态-预测分离始终能带来更好的数据效率和计算效率，降低了验证损失，并在下游任务上平均比标准 Transformer 高出 2-3 个百分点。我们还进行了广泛的实证分析，排除了潜在的混杂因素，并证明了我们的设计在梯度上所体现出的根本性差异。
tldr: 该论文提出“状态-预测分离假设”，设计了一种用独立计算流将“预测下一个token”与“存储状态”两种功能解耦的 Transformer 变体，多规模预训练实验表明其具有更高的数据与计算效率，在下游任务上平均超越标准 Transformer 2-3 个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the state-prediction separation hypothesis and designs a Transformer variant that uses separate computation streams to decouple next-token prediction from state storage, demonstrating improved data and compute efficiency across scales and outperforming standard Transformers by 2-3 percentage points on average on downstream tasks.
